# The creation of Superman

Superman was created by writer Jerry Siegel and artist Joe Shuster, two friends from Cleveland, Ohio. The character first appeared in Action Comics #1, published in 1938 by the company that later became DC Comics.

Siegel and Shuster had tried to sell the idea for several years before it was accepted. Action Comics #1 was a huge success, and Superman is widely seen as the character who started the superhero genre and the Golden Age of comic books.

The creators sold the rights to Superman for a small sum, and they later fought long legal battles over credit and payment. In the 1970s, after public pressure, the publisher agreed to give them a yearly pension and restore their creator credit.
